facts.fact_text: An EU-Russia summit was scheduled for 17 and 18 May 2007 to take place in Samara.
On 18 May 2007 the applicant was travelling to Samara to take part in the opposition rally called 'March of Dissent'.
The opposition rally 'March of Dissent' had been organised to coincide with the EU-Russia summit scheduled for 17 and 18 May 2007 in Samara.
The applicant was accompanied by several activists who were also travelling to the 'March of Dissent' rally in Samara on 18 May 2007.
The applicant submits that, when he presented his passport for identity check, police officer A. seized the applicant's passport.
The applicant submits that, when he presented his passport for identity check, police officer A. seized the applicant's ticket.
The applicant submits that he was required to leave the check-in area and to follow police officer A.
The applicant submits that he was taken to a police office on the second floor of Sheremetyevo airport.
The applicant submits that five other persons from his group were escorted from the check-in hall in the same manner as the applicant.
At 11.20 a.m. on 18 May 2007, the applicant and the five others from his group were ordered to remain on the second floor of Sheremetyevo airport.
At 11.20 a.m. on 18 May 2007, the applicant and the five others from his group were informed that they would have to be questioned as to how they had purchased their allegedly forged tickets.
The applicant maintains that he was under orders not to leave the police office at Sheremetyevo airport.
The applicant maintains that he was prevented from leaving the police office at Sheremetyevo airport by an armed policeman who was guarding the doorway.
On the pro forma statement (объяснение), the applicant has written that from 8.30 a.m. until 12.50 p.m. on 18 May 2007 he had been deprived of his freedom of movement.

The handwritten declaration states that on 18 May 2007 at Sheremetyevo Airport Terminal 1, the applicant and five others were prevented from taking flight 813 to Samara because police officer A. seized their tickets at the check-in desk.
The handwritten declaration states that the applicant and five others were at the airport building under the surveillance of police officers, with their passports confiscated.

The handwritten declaration states that at 11.20 a.m. on 18 May 2007, police officers A., C. and S. categorically prohibited the applicant and five others from leaving the second floor of Sheremetyevo airport.

Section 11(4) of the Police Act (no. 1026-1 of 18 April 1991), as in force at the material time, provided that, for the performance of their duties, the police had the right to obtain from citizens and State officials necessary statements, information, certificates, documents and copies thereof.

Article 27.7 of the Code of Administrative Offences allows personal searches and searches of luggage carried by a person to be conducted if it is necessary to find an object or an instrument of an administrative offence.
Article 27.7 of the Code of Administrative Offences defines the search procedure and sets out the requirements of the search report.

Article 27.10 of the Code of Administrative Offences states that objects and instruments of an administrative offence, as well as documents that may serve as evidence in proceedings concerning an administrative offence, may be seized in accordance with the specified procedure.
Article 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the Russian Federation entered into force on 1 July 2002.

Article 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the Russian Federation provides that any decisions and actions (or failures to act) by investigators, investigating judges or prosecutors with regard to a criminal investigation may be challenged before a superior prosecutor or a court.
The Government submitted that on 17 May 2007, the Department of the Interior's Sheremetyevo airport branch received information on forged tickets being sold for the 18 May 2007 Moscow-Samara flight.

The Government submitted that on 18 May 2007, officers from the Department of the Interior's Sheremetyevo airport branch, acting on information about forged tickets, were present at check-in and examined the tickets of all passengers on the Moscow-Samara flight.
The Government submitted that in the course of the ticket checks on 18 May 2007, twenty tickets bearing signs of forgery were found, having worn spots and dubious printing forms.
When questioned, police officer A. stated that on 17 May 2007 at 6 p.m. he received operative information that some forged tickets had been sold for the Moscow-Samara flight leaving on 18 May 2007.

When questioned, the Head of the Operational-Search Unit of the Aviation Division of the Department of the Interior, officer S., stated that on 18 May 2007, on the occasion of the high-profile EU-Russia summit in Samara, policemen of the Aviation Division of the Moscow branch of the Department of the Interior, together with its subordinate units in the airports of the Moscow region, carried out operational search activities to identify persons of an extremist nature intending to organise mass riots.
Officer S. stated that in connection with the operational search activities, the police carried out checks on persons leaving for Samara on 18 May 2007.

The prosecutor's office decision of 28 June 2007 stated that on 18 May 2007 the police, together with the Sheremetyevo airport security service, carried out a check of the passengers leaving on flight no. 813, Moscow–Samara.

When questioned, the Head of the Operational-Search Unit of the Aviation Division of the Department of the Interior, officer S., stated that on 18 May 2007, on the occasion of the high-profile EU-Russia summit in Samara, policemen of the Aviation Division of the Moscow branch of the Department of the Interior, together with its subordinate units in the airports of the Moscow region, carried out operational search activities to identify persons of an extremist nature intending to organise mass riots.
Officer S. stated that in connection with the operational search activities, the police carried out checks on persons leaving for Samara on 18 May 2007.
Officer S. stated that several passengers decided not to fly on flight no. 813, Moscow–Samara, without explaining why.
The prosecutor's office inquiry established that the policemen had acted within their powers and with sufficient grounds when seizing the tickets of the passengers for flight no. 813, Moscow–Samara.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant had been taken to the airport police quarters to provide an explanation for the purchase of his ticket.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant had not been 'isolated' at the police station at Sheremetyevo airport.

The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that there had been no grounds for applying the three-hour time-limit for the application of preventative measures in administrative offences cases as provided for by the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that there had been no grounds for the drawing up of a detention report (протокол о задержании).
